subject.title: Anthropic setup-token onboarding path has multiple failure modes (docs gap, credential propagation, multi-agent sync)

question: Should Anthropic setup-token onboarding explicitly copy static token profiles into each configured agent store, or should OpenClaw keep the current main-store read-through model and focus this issue on setup-token UX and validation?
rationale: The code no longer needs sibling copies for the common runtime read path, but the issue and linked PR propose credential duplication across agent stores, which changes credential blast radius and upgrade/security behavior.

options.title: Prefer inheritance plus UX validation
options.body: Keep credentials in the selected/default auth store, add clearer setup-token guidance and post-write/status validation, and avoid copying secrets across sibling agents by default.

options.title: Approve explicit static-token sibling sync
options.body: Allow setup-token/paste-token to copy portable static token profiles into configured sibling agents with focused tests and security-facing docs.

options.title: Close in favor of current behavior
options.body: Treat current SQLite plus main-store inheritance as sufficient and ask for a new live reproduction for any remaining setup-token failures.

recommendation.title: Prefer inheritance plus UX validation
recommendation.body: Keep credentials in the selected/default auth store, add clearer setup-token guidance and post-write/status validation, and avoid copying secrets across sibling agents by default.
